drivers.name: 30% off promotion
drivers.evidence: Deeper than past promotions (max 25%); historical lift in similar event was x1.68 (2026-08-03), though seasonally boosted. Noise-adjusted average lift is x1.02, but price drop is 27.1%, suggesting stronger lift. Shrink to +5% due to uncertainty and noisy history.

drivers.name: Competitor store opening
drivers.evidence: New competitor across the street may divert shoppers. No direct data, but plausible downside. A competitor move in a similar category led to 10% demand loss. Conservative shrink due to single event.

adjustment.analysis: The 30% off promotion is deeper than past promotions (max 25% in 2025), and the product has shown strong lift during similar events (x1.68 in 2026-08-03, though seasonally boosted). The noise-adjusted uplift from past promotions is only x1.02, but this week's price drop is more aggressive. A competitor opening across the street may draw shoppers away, lowering demand. The baseline already reflects seasonal decline (trend -21.9% over 13 weeks). The classical model's 1.02 is too low given the price shock. Adjust upward modestly, but account for competitive threat and thin evidence. Shrink toward 1.0 due to limited comparable promotions.

PRODUCT: Sunscreen SPF50 | category Personal Care | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-22 (6 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: Promotion: 30% off
  shelf price: 9.75 (-27.1% vs regular price 13.38)
  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 24.9 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 64.6 | 10%-90%: 1.6 - 44.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
